subject: design-technology
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A major social impact of factory automation on a community can be:
questions.explain: Replacing workers with machines can reduce employment, affecting workers and the surrounding community.

questions.q: A rechargeable battery stores energy in which form?
questions.explain: A battery stores energy chemically and converts it to electrical energy when it discharges through a circuit.

questions.q: Choosing a material that can be recycled at the end of a product's life supports sustainability by:
options: Keeping materials in use and reducing demand for new raw resources
Increasing the amount of waste sent to landfill
Making the product impossible to dispose of
Guaranteeing the product never wears out
questions.explain: Recyclable materials can be recovered and reprocessed, reducing landfill and the need to extract new raw materials.

questions.q: Fairtrade certification aims primarily to:
options: Make products as cheap as possible for shops
Ensure producers in developing countries receive fair prices and conditions
questions.explain: Fairtrade ensures producers, often farmers in developing countries, receive a fair, stable price and decent working conditions.

questions.q: Using recycled aluminium instead of new aluminium is beneficial because it:
options: Uses far less energy than extracting new metal from ore
questions.explain: Recycling aluminium uses only a small fraction of the energy needed to extract and refine new aluminium from ore.

questions.q: Reducing the number of different materials in a product can improve sustainability because it:
options: Makes the product harder to take apart
Makes separating and recycling the materials easier at end of life
questions.explain: Using fewer, easily separated materials makes a product simpler to disassemble and recycle at the end of its life.

questions.q: Designing a product so it can be easily taken apart at end of life is called design for:
questions.explain: Design for disassembly makes products easy to take apart so parts can be repaired, reused or recycled.

questions.q: A product life cycle assessment considers the impact of a product:
options: Only while it is being used
Only at the point of sale
From raw material extraction through manufacture, use and disposal
questions.explain: A life cycle assessment evaluates environmental impact across the whole life: extraction, processing, manufacture, distribution, use and disposal.

questions.q: 'Reduce' in the 6 Rs encourages designers and users to:
options: Use more material to be safe
Use less material and energy to make and run a product
questions.explain: Reduce focuses on minimising the amount of material and energy used in making and using a product.

questions.q: Recycling differs from reusing because recycling:
options: Processes a material to make a new product
Refuses to use the material at all
Uses a product again in its current form
questions.explain: Recycling reprocesses a material into raw form to make a new product, whereas reusing keeps the original item in use as it is.

questions.q: A finite (non-renewable) resource is one that:
options: Can be replaced as fast as it is used
Will eventually run out because it is used faster than it forms
questions.explain: Finite resources such as oil and metals form very slowly and will eventually be depleted as we use them up.

questions.q: An ethical concern when sourcing materials globally is:
options: Making the product as colourful as possible
Ensuring workers are paid fairly and not exploited
questions.explain: Ethical sourcing considers whether the people who extract or make materials are treated and paid fairly.

questions.q: 'Repair' as one of the 6 Rs is more sustainable than replacing because it:
options: Extends a product's life and saves the resources of making a new one
Always costs more than a new product
Sends the product to landfill sooner
questions.explain: Repairing a product keeps it in use for longer, saving the energy and raw materials needed to manufacture a replacement.

questions.q: Which of the following is one of the 6 Rs of sustainability?
questions.explain: The 6 Rs are reduce, reuse, recycle, refuse, rethink and repair; 'rethink' encourages designing in more sustainable ways.

questions.q: Planned obsolescence refers to designing products that:
options: Are deliberately made to have a limited useful life so they are replaced sooner
Last as long as technically possible
questions.explain: Planned obsolescence is the practice of designing products with a limited lifespan to encourage repeat purchases.

questions.q: In the 6 Rs of sustainability, 'Refuse' means to:
options: Decline to buy or use something you do not really need
Recycle the material into something new
questions.explain: Refuse means choosing not to buy or use products or materials that are unnecessary or wasteful in the first place.

questions.q: Which of these is a non-renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Coal is a finite fossil fuel that cannot be replenished, unlike the renewable sources solar, hydro and wind.

questions.q: The Arts and Crafts movement, associated with William Morris, is known for valuing:
options: Traditional craftsmanship and quality natural materials
questions.explain: The Arts and Crafts movement championed traditional craftsmanship, natural materials and quality over cheap industrial mass production.

questions.q: The 'circular economy' aims to:
options: Throw products away as fast as possible
Keep materials and products in use for as long as possible, designing out waste
questions.explain: A circular economy keeps resources in use through reuse, repair and recycling, designing out waste rather than discarding products.

questions.q: An environmental consequence of sending products to landfill is that:
options: Materials are lost and may release pollutants as they break down
questions.explain: Landfill wastes the embedded resources and can release pollutants and greenhouse gases as waste decomposes.

questions.q: Which is an example of a new or emerging technology used in modern manufacturing?
questions.explain: Additive manufacturing such as 3D printing is a newer technology transforming how prototypes and products are made.

questions.q: Which of these is a renewable energy source?
questions.explain: Wind is a renewable source that naturally replenishes, unlike the finite fossil fuels coal, gas and oil.
